stories.title: CRE Loan Delinquencies Decline in Q2; CMBS Remains Elevated
stories.excerpt: Delinquency rates for mortgages backed by commercial properties decreased during the second quarter of 2026. That’s according to the Mortgage Bankers Association’s (MBA) latest commercial real estate finance (CREF) Loan Performance Survey, which reported that CMBS delinquencies declined during Q2 but remain elevated relative to other lender types. The survey found that the share of loans that were delinquent generally declined across the major property types, though performance remained mixed. Office and lodging continued to exhibit the highest delinquency rates. CMBS delinquencies fell by 39 basis points to 4.82% during the quarter. The second-highest delinquency rate was for life company loans, which also saw an improvement during Q2, falling 28 bps to 1.19%. “Commercial mortgage loan performance improved during the second quarter, with delinquency rates declining across most major property types and capital sources,” said Reggie Booker, MBA’s associate VP of commercial real estate research. “While office and lodging properties continue to face challenges and CMBS delinquency rates remain elevated relative to other lenders, the overall decline in non-current loan balances points to continued stability in the commercial mortgage market.” The post CRE Loan Delinquencies Decline in Q2; CMBS Remains Elevated appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CMBS delinquencies fell 39 bps to 4.82% in Q2 2026; remain elevated vs. other lenders.
Office and lodging show highest delinquency rates; life company loans improved 28 bps to 1.19%.
Overall CRE loan performance improved; non-current balances declining across most property types.
stories.summary: Commercial mortgage delinquencies declined in Q2 2026, with CMBS rates falling 39 basis points to 4.82% and life company loans improving 28 bps to 1.19%. Office and lodging properties continue to face the most stress with elevated delinquency rates. The decline in non-current balances signals stabilization in CRE lending, though CMBS remains elevated relative to traditional lenders.
stories.impact: Improving multifamily-focused lender health (life companies, portfolio lenders) expands debt availability and reduces refinancing friction for apartment acquisitions and development projects. However, persistent office distress may free up developer capital and lender appetite for redeployment into multifamily-friendly markets and sponsors with strong underwriting track records.

stories.title: Return to Lender: Week of July 30, 2026
stories.excerpt: A historic downtown Denver office building once set to receive millions in public incentives for a residential conversion has hit the market following a foreclosure, reported the Denver Business Journal. The Symes Building, at 820 16th St., was listed for sale as a bank-owned foreclosure and redevelopment opportunity with “complete vacancy.” Canyon Law, a listing agent for Kenai Capital Advisors, which is acting on behalf of owner Thorofare Capital, said the last tenant vacated in March, leaving the building empty. The Boston Business Journal reported that a Howard Johnson Inn in Williamstown, MA, one of six remaining locations in the state where the chain was founded in 1925, is scheduled for a foreclosure auction. Auction firm Aaron Posnik & Co. has scheduled an auction for Aug. 6, following the foreclosure by lender Beacon Bank. The K&L Gates Center in downtown Pittsburgh is on the market, with a Newmark team offering the Liberty Avenue building in a “receivership sale,” reported the Pittsburgh Business Times. The firm launches marketing for the 43% leased building after the building’s namesake tenant, the law firm K&L Gates, announced it would keep its office there in January 2025. It did so a little more than a year after the property’s ownership, One Oliver Associates LP, majority-owned by Chilean pension fund Independencia Asset Management, was forced into default by lender Pacific Life. A loan modification has failed to materialize on The Club Row Building loan ($155.0 million | JPMBB 2015-C27 & JPMBB 2015-C28), reported Morningstar Credit. This marks the second time a modification neared the finish line only to be scrapped at the last minute. The loan, backed by a 369,000-square-foot office building on W. 44th Street between 5th Avenue and 6th Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, moved to special servicing in January 2025 after missing its maturity. stories.title: Vici Properties Is Standing By to Build a Las Vegas NBA Arena
stories.excerpt: Vici Properties executives during a Thursday morning earnings call teased the possibility of building a National Basketball Association (NBA) arena complex on land the company owns in Las Vegas. In addition to being the largest owner on the Las Vegas Strip with properties including the Venetian, Mandalay Bay, the MGM Grand and Caesars Palace, the Manhattan-based Vici also controls several dozen undeveloped acres behind the Planet Hollywood, Paris and Horseshoe casinos. The NBA toward the start of 2026 began formally reviewing the possibility of adding a Las Vegas franchise. The move highlighted what Vici President and Chief Operating Officer John Payne noted on the earnings call was the “massive growth in pro sports” in Las Vegas. Major League Baseball’s Oakland A’s are relocating to Las Vegas, and the city in the past 10 years has added National Football League, National Hockey League and Women’s National Basketball Association teams. Nothing is finalized regarding developing an NBA arena complex, despite weeks of media speculation. Executives on the second-quarter earnings call did not discuss any moves in depth. The addition of such a complex, though, would fit into the strategy of a company that bills itself as an “experiential real estate investment trust.” Its 103-property portfolio inside and outside of Las Vegas is capitalizing on a particularly robust era for experiential retail. The market for experiential retail globally is expected to more than quadruple from the $132 billion it stood at toward the start of 2026, according to market research firm Metatech Insights. Heck, one of the fastest-growing commercial real estate asset classes in the U.S. and Canada is trampoline parks. (Ed Pitoniak, Vici’s CEO, told Commercial Observer in April 2025 that when he mastered the experiential retail approach, “I tell people I died and went to business heaven.”) Vici’s second-quarter numbers reflected the boom times. bullets: Vici Properties teasing NBA arena development on undeveloped Las Vegas Strip land.
MLB Oakland A's relocating to Las Vegas; NFL, NHL, WNBA teams added past 10 years.
Pro sports expansion drives 'massive growth' in Las Vegas; no deal finalized yet.
stories.summary: Vici Properties CEO Ed Pitoniak mentioned the possibility of developing an NBA arena complex on undeveloped land the company controls behind Planet Hollywood, Paris, and Horseshoe casinos in Las Vegas. The city has added MLB, NFL, NHL, and WNBA franchises in the past decade, signaling rapid sports and entertainment-led growth. No deal has been finalized despite weeks of media speculation.
stories.impact: Major sports venue development acts as a primary demand generator for service-sector employment and visitor/resident population in Las Vegas. A new NBA arena accelerates the metro's already-strong hospitality and entertainment labor absorption, driving ancillary job creation and sustained in-migration—particularly attractive for multifamily developers targeting Las Vegas submarkets with high daily-rate employment density and younger demographic inflow. Timing of entitlement and construction could unlock mid-term rental demand growth (2028–2030).

stories.title: Mezcali Founders to Open New Fusion Concept in Financial District
stories.excerpt: The restaurateurs behind Mexican restaurant Mezcali and American tavern the Malt House have signed a lease for a new food concept in Manhattan’s Financial District. Eoin Foyle and Darren Shore signed a 20-year, 4,744-square-foot lease in the retail component of TF Cornerstone’s 2 Gold Street, where they will launch their latest brainchild, a Hawaiian-Caribbean-Asian fusion restaurant called Solerum, according to the landlord. TF Cornerstone did not immediately disclose the asking rent for the space, but the average retail asking rent for retail space on the nearby corridor of Broadway from Battery Park to Chambers Street was $224 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “As the Financial District continues to evolve into one of New York City’s most dynamic mixed-use neighborhoods, we’re committed to curating a retail experience that enhances the everyday lives of our residents, while serving the broader community,” Steve Gonzalez, vice president of retail leasing at TF Cornerstone, said in a statement. “Solerum’s distinctive concept and hospitality-driven dining experience make it an excellent addition to the neighborhood.” Manu Wendum and John DiGangi of Retail by MONA negotiated on behalf of the tenant, while Steven Baker, Daniyel Cohen and Tom Galo of RTL Partners represented TF Cornerstone in the deal. Retail by MONA and Baker did not immediately respond to requests for comment. “The opening of Solerum at 2 Gold Street represents our continued investment in New York City and the Financial District, a neighborhood that has played an important role in the growth of our restaurant business,” Foyle said in a statement. 2 Gold Street sits between Maiden Lane and Platt Street, across the street from Mezcali at 83 Maiden Lane and three blocks from the Malt House at 9 Maiden Lane. The Malt House also has a location at 206 Thompson Street in Greenwich Village. The Gold Street pro
bullets: Mezcali founders sign 20-year, 4,744-sf retail lease in Manhattan Financial District.
TF Cornerstone's 2 Gold Street; average Broadway retail asking rent $224/sf in Q2 2026.
Specialty F&B tenant signals Financial District evolution into mixed-use residential neighborhood.
stories.summary: Restaurateurs Eoin Foyle and Darren Shore signed a 20-year, 4,744-square-foot lease for a new Hawaiian-Caribbean-Asian fusion concept called Solerum at TF Cornerstone's 2 Gold Street in Manhattan's Financial District. Retail asking rents on nearby Broadway (Battery Park to Chambers) averaged $224/sf in Q2 2026. The landlord characterized the Financial District as evolving into a dynamic mixed-use neighborhood.
stories.impact: Financial District retail leasing velocity and rent-paying tenant quality (established restaurant group, long-term lease) validate the submarket's residential-amenity value proposition. Strong F&B anchoring supports the fundamentals for new multifamily development and conversion projects in lower Manhattan, signaling sufficient daytime and evening density to support residential conversion feasibility and renter retention in this historically office-dependent zone.

stories.title: X Capital Developing Melissa Mixed-Use Project
stories.excerpt: X Capital has started work on a mixed-use development in Melissa, just outside McKinney. The Dallas Business Journal reports the company is bringing new retail and office space to the fast-growing city. And apartments may be down the road. Infrastructure work has begun on the first phase of Melissa Park Village, a 22-acre development at the northeast corner of State Highway 121 and Melissa Road. The first phase will include 36,000 square feet of retail space across two buildings, along with a two-story, 23,000-square-foot building designed for office space and ground-floor retail. The first buildings are expected to be completed in 2027. Weitzman’s Emilie Paulson, Maggie Hansen and Addison Gragson are leasing the retail and office space. Scott Smith and Corbin Tanenbaum are marketing land within the development for future apartments. The city ranked as the nation’s fourth-fastest-growing city after its population increased nearly 15% to more than 29,000 residents. The post X Capital Developing Melissa Mixed-Use Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: X Capital developing 22-acre Melissa Park Village near McKinney, Texas; infrastructure started.
Phase 1: 36,000 sf retail + 23,000 sf office/retail; completion 2027. Land for future apartments.
Melissa ranked 4th-fastest-growing U.S. city; population grew nearly 15% to 29,000+ residents.
stories.summary: X Capital has begun infrastructure work on Melissa Park Village, a 22-acre mixed-use development in Melissa just outside McKinney, Texas. Phase 1 includes 36,000 sf of retail across two buildings and a 23,000 sf office/ground-floor retail building due in 2027. Brokers are marketing land within the development for future apartments. Melissa was ranked the nation's 4th-fastest-growing city with nearly 15% population growth to over 29,000 residents.
stories.impact: Melissa's ranking as 4th-fastest-growing U.S. city and 15% recent population growth signal strong household formation and migration inflow exceeding regional averages. Staged retail/office-first approach with explicitly reserved apartment land indicates developer confidence in near-term demand absorption. Dallas-Fort Worth exurban markets like Melissa are prime targets for junior-market multifamily development; this project's phasing suggests 2027–2028 apartment delivery window aligned with peak population inflection.

stories.title: Torchlight Investment Provides $52M Acquisition Debt, Equity for Indianapolis Asset
stories.excerpt: Hudson Investing has secured $52.1 million in acquisition financing for Maple Knoll Apartments, a 300-unit garden-style multifamily complex just outside Indianapolis, Ind., Commercial Observer can first report. Torchlight Investment provided the equity, while Northmarq structured the full capital stack for the transaction, providing the senior debt directly through Northmarq’s in-house Freddie Mac platform. A Northmarq team of Annamarie Bjorklund and Cody Field arranged the transaction. Bjorklund said in a statement that Northmarq was able to secure both the debt and equity from Torchlight due to Hudson’s reputation as “a disciplined, well-capitalized sponsor.” “We knew as soon as we met the Hudson team and saw their plan for the asset that they would be a natural fit,” Bjorklund said. “Ultimately, Torchlight stood out, and we’re excited for their new partnership and to see the next chapter for a great property.” Located at 500 Bigleaf Maple Way in Westfield, a city 20 miles north of Downtown Indianapolis, Maple Knoll Apartments opened in 2007 and features 18 three-story apartment buildings across 24 acres, all of which contain one- to three-bedroom units. Hudson Investing is purchasing the property from an unnamed institutional insurance company, but previous owners include Blackstone and GE Capital. The acquisition is part of Hudson’s value-add strategy, and the firm plans to invest capital to renovate the entire property, according to a release from Northmarq. “We continue to see Indianapolis as a highly attractive investment market with strong population growth, quality employment drivers and desirable suburban communities that continue to attract residents,” said Kent Ritter, CEO of Hudson Investing. bullets: Hudson Investing closed $52.1M financing for 300-unit Maple Knoll Apartments, Westfield, Ind.
Torchlight Investment provided equity; Northmarq sourced senior debt via Freddie Mac platform.
Asset in suburbs north of Indianapolis; disciplined sponsor reputation enabled single-source capital stack.
stories.summary: Hudson Investing secured $52.1 million in acquisition financing for Maple Knoll Apartments, a 300-unit garden-style complex in Westfield, Indiana (20 miles north of Downtown Indianapolis). Torchlight Investment provided equity while Northmarq sourced senior debt through its Freddie Mac platform. The transaction was arranged by Northmarq's Annamarie Bjorklund and Cody Field, who cited Hudson's reputation as a disciplined sponsor as key to securing both debt and equity from a single source.
stories.impact: Torchlight Investment's willingness to package debt and equity for a secondary-market suburban Indianapolis asset demonstrates continued capital availability for stabilized, well-sponsored multifamily acquisitions outside primary markets. Strong sponsor track record and asset quality are now table stakes for GSE-backed financing; this validates acquisition and value-add strategies in Midwest I-4 and Sunbelt tier-2 metros where population migration and job growth support absorption fundamentals.

stories.title: Growing Richmond Lands Sam’s Club
stories.excerpt: Richmond, south and west of Houston, is a town of just over 11,000 residents, but like a lot of other Texas towns, its growing. So much so that a development team is considering building a mixed-use project that includes a Sam’s Club warehouse store. Called Circle Oak, the George Foundation recently sold the land to Park Collective Retail Partners to build the Sam’s Club, at a cost of $51 million. The Houston Business Journal reports Park Collective also plans to build a 19,600-square-foot multitenant retail building and is negotiating leases with potential pad site users for three or four sites along FM 762. The George Foundation says there is also plenty of space for restaurant, retail or office ground leases on both sides of the freeway. The site is across from NewQuest’s 2 million-square-foot Brazos Town Center. The Circle Oak site is just a few miles north of the 19,500-acre George Ranch, which has been in the George family’s possession for generations. The post Growing Richmond Lands Sam’s Club appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Park Collective Retail Partners acquired land in Richmond, Texas for $51M Sam's Club project.
Circle Oak development: Sam's Club + 19,600 sf multitenant retail; pad sites and dining negotiated.
Richmond (11,000+ residents) is fast-growing Texas town; site across from 2M sf Brazos Town Center.
stories.summary: Park Collective Retail Partners acquired land in Richmond, Texas (just south and west of Houston) from the George Foundation for $51 million to develop Circle Oak, anchored by a Sam's Club warehouse store. The project also includes a 19,600-square-foot multitenant retail building and negotiated pad-site leases for restaurants and retail. The George Foundation notes ample space for additional retail, office, and ground leases on both sides of the freeway, adjacent to NewQuest's 2 million-square-foot Brazos Town Center.
stories.impact: Large-format retail anchors (Sam's Club) drive anchor-tenant validation and co-tenancy risk reduction, making adjacent land parcels attractive for multifamily, hospitality, or mixed-use infill. Richmond's rapid growth and proximity to NewQuest's major retail center create a high-density suburban node; multifamily developers should monitor for future pad-site or ground-lease opportunities as the retail shell stabilizes and market maturity warrants residential or office conversion parcels (2027+).

stories.title: Rock Architecture & Engineering Expands to 4K SF at GFP’s 630 Ninth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Architecture firm Rock Architecture & Engineering has signed a 3,835-square-foot deal to extend and expand its presence at GFP Real Estate’s 630 Ninth Avenue, the landlord announced Thursday. The firm, which specializes in building restoration projects and gets its name from a focus on solid foundations, will move from the sixth floor to the 10th floor of the 13-story office property. It’s a three-year lease amendment, according to GFP. The firm did not disclose the asking rent. However, the average asking rent for office space in Midtown was $84.99 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026, according to data from Colliers. The tenant did not work with a broker on this deal, according to GFP, while the landlord was represented in-house by Matthew Mandell. Additionally, software and media company Neoteny Studios signed a two-year, 1,247-square-foot lease at 630 Ninth Avenue for its new headquarters. Neoteny also did not work with a broker on this transaction. GFP’s Mandell represented the landlord on this deal as well. “These transactions demonstrate the continued appeal of well-priced, efficient office space for both growing companies and existing tenants looking to expand,” Mandell said in a statement. “630 Ninth Avenue continues to attract businesses that value convenience, flexibility and quality space in a highly accessible Midtown location.” Also known as the Film Center Building, 630 Ninth Avenue is situated between West 44th and West 45th streets. Tenants in the building include live theater and entertainment company ATG Entertainment, citizen-run government advisory board Manhattan Community Advisory Board 4 and video production services agency CRC Media. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Rock Architecture & Engineering expands 3,835 sf at GFP's 630 Ninth Avenue, Midtown Manhattan.
3-year lease amendment; move from 6th to 10th floor. Midtown office asking rent ~$85/sf Q2 2026.
Specialty tenant (building restoration) signals selective office leasing by niche professional services.
stories.summary: Rock Architecture & Engineering signed a 3,835-square-foot lease expansion at GFP Real Estate's 630 Ninth Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, moving from the 6th to the 10th floor on a three-year amendment. Average asking rent for Midtown office space was $84.99/sf in Q2 2026. The firm specializes in building restoration; no broker was involved in the transaction.
stories.impact: Limited direct impact on multifamily development. However, selective office tenant renewals by specialized professional services (architecture, engineering) at mid-tier Midtown rents (~$85/sf) indicate selective office demand recovery driven by niche sectors, not broad-based return-to-office. Developers should note that Manhattan office-to-residential conversion economics remain dependent on high-density, high-income residential demand rather than office market normalization.

stories.title: Joint Venture Inks $81M Acquisition Loan for Denver-Area Apartments
stories.excerpt: The Dinerstein Cos. and PGIM closed on an $81 million refinancing loan for Atlas Peakview, a 330-unit multifamily community in Centennial. Mesa West Capital funded the loan in a deal arranged by Walker & Dunlop. Multihousing News reports that Atlas Peakview was delivered in 2025 and has since reached 85 percent occupancy. The project previously received $76.8 million in construction financing from Texas Capital Bank in 2021. The community features studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments with two- and three-bedroom townhomes available for rent. Each residence features in-unit laundry, walk-in closets, smart locks and Energy Star-certified appliances. Average monthly rent at Atlas Peakview is approximately $2,280,. Residents have access to shared amenities including a swimming pool, an outdoor kitchen, a fitness center, a two-story coworking space, a speakeasy and a pet-wash station. Walker & Dunlop’s Tom Melody, Paul House and John Melody arranged the financing. The post Joint Venture Inks $81M Acquisition Loan for Denver-Area Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Dinerstein Cos. and PGIM closed $81M refinance for 330-unit Atlas Peakview, Centennial, Colorado.
Asset delivered 2025, reached 85% occupancy; avg. rent ~$2,280/month; studio to 3-bed units.
Mesa West Capital funded loan; Walker & Dunlop arranged. Previous construction loan $76.8M (2021).
stories.summary: The Dinerstein Cos. and PGIM closed an $81 million refinancing loan for Atlas Peakview, a 330-unit multifamily community in Centennial, Colorado (Denver metro). The project was delivered in 2025 and has reached 85% occupancy with average monthly rent at approximately $2,280. The asset was previously financed with a $76.8 million construction loan from Texas Capital Bank in 2021. Mesa West Capital funded the refinance, arranged by Walker & Dunlop.
stories.impact: Strong occupancy (85% within one year of delivery) and successful refinancing at elevated pricing validate Denver-metro suburban multifamily fundamentals and sponsor execution quality. Ability to refinance recent stabilized assets signals continued debt availability for well-leased projects; developers with near-stabilization assets in Denver-area submarkets (Centennial, Littleton, Aurora) should accelerate lease-up and refinancing strategies in next 12 months before potential rate cap increases limit refi upside.

stories.title: Trove Partners’ Ian Slater on New York’s Pied-a-Terre Tax and Owners’ First Moves
stories.excerpt: Last week, the Mamdani administration made good on its promise to enact a tax on New York City’s wealthiest homeowners. The city’s Department of Finance published an online database of more than 31,000 properties and property owners who might be subject to a new pied-a-terre tax. When the surcharge passed in May, city and state officials initially estimated roughly 10,000 properties would be subject to the tax. While the list sent out last week doesn’t represent the final roundup of homes set to face higher levies, it does include several notable addresses — and notable homeowners. Among the numerous billionaires, CEOs and business leaders on the list are Citadel CEO Ken Griffin — somewhat of a given — “Shark Tank” investor Mark Cuban, IMAX CEO Richard Gelfond and Blackstone CEO and co-founder Stephen Schwarzman. Several A-list celebrities also made the list, including fashion icon Anna Wintour, actor Cynthia Nixon, singer Taylor Swift, filmmaker Woody Allen and actor Alan Cumming. Former New York Times critic Nicolai Ouroussoff, international art dealer David Zwirner and journalist Julie Satow were also notable mentions. As for properties, prominent luxury residential buildings and developments on Mamdani’s list included the Jenga Tower at 56 Leonard Street in Tribeca, Witkoff Group’s 150 Charles Street in the West Village, MetroLoft’s 443 Greenwich Street in Tribeca, Vornado Realty Trust’s 220 Central Park South on Billionaires’ Row, the One57 condo tower in Midtown, and 15 Central Park West in Lincoln Square. 220 Central Park South. bullets: NYC pied-à-terre tax enforcement: 31,000+ properties initially identified; originally estimated ~10,000.
High-profile owners on list: Ken Griffin, Taylor Swift, Mark Cuban, Stephen Schwarzman, others.
Tax published; final assessment and collection timeline remain unclear; incentivizes property sales/repurposing.
stories.summary: New York City's Mamdani administration published an online database of over 31,000 properties subject to a new pied-à-terre tax on wealthy homeowners, significantly exceeding the original estimate of ~10,000 properties. The list includes notable billionaires (Ken Griffin, Stephen Schwarzman), celebrities (Taylor Swift, Mark Cuban), and cultural figures. The tax passed in May; the published list represents an initial draft, with final assessments and collection timelines still pending.
stories.impact: Pied-à-terre tax enforcement at 3x initial volume signals aggressive revenue capture and potential forced liquidations of secondary residences in Manhattan and outer boroughs over 2–3 years. Developers should monitor for uptick in distressed single-family brownstone or condo sales in prime residential neighborhoods (Upper East Side, Brooklyn Heights, Park Slope), creating potential conversion or assemblage opportunities for boutique multifamily redevelopment. Tax-induced supply of trophy properties may also suppress luxury condo valuations and shift capital toward stabilized rental assets.
